correctness.rationale: Cauchy-Kubota normalization gives δ1(B,P)=1/2∫_0^{2π}|1-h_P(u)|dθ when P contains the disk center. On each convex-polygon vertex normal cone (0<α<π), h=a cos x+b sin x. A signed dual witness with switches at ±asin(sin(α/2)/2) annihilates both cosine and sine, proving local error ≥g(α)=α-4asin(sin(α/2)/2); equality forces b=0,a=sec(switch). The explicitly positive g and Jensen show sum g(α_i)≥N g(2π/N) for m<=N. Local equality and equal normal gaps force the unique centered regular N-gon at radius (1-sin²(π/N)/4)^-1/2. Direct symbolic expansion yields π³/(8N²)+π⁵/(128N⁴)-17π⁷/(15360N⁶)+... . Degenerate normal cones are excluded by counting genuine extreme vertices; the N=3 boundary remains α=2π/3<π.

value.rationale: A complete sharp approximation problem for a natural projection-based intrinsic-volume metric, for every finite vertex count, with equality classification and nontrivial optimal scaling between inscribed and circumscribed polygons. The argument supplies a reusable support-function signed witness, and improves beyond the previously known regular triangle example and general asymptotic-rate bounds.

limitations: Full-dimensional convex planar polygons containing disk center; at most N vertices, N>=3; cannot assert arbitrary-position, other metrics or higher dimensions.
Exact disk support approximation has extensive classical literature; an unknown all-N equivalent is possible under L1 approximation vocabulary.
